united-states/mokelumne-river.text: Lodi's largest sub-appellation, in northern San Joaquin County, California, on alluvial fan soils of sand and loam. It is the historic home of Lodi's oldest vines, including old head-trained Zinfandel, Carignan and Cinsaut.

united-states/monterey.text: A long Central Coast AVA running from Monterey Bay south through the Salinas Valley. The north is cool with a very long growing season, and Chardonnay is the leading grape. Pinot Noir and Riesling grow nearer the cold Pacific, and Bordeaux grapes in the warmer south.

united-states/moon-mountain-district-son.text: A mountainous Sonoma Valley AVA on the western slopes of the Mayacamas, with a long reputation for rich, intensely flavored Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah dating to the 1880s. About 1,500 acres of vines sit among its hills and ridges.

united-states/mount-pisgah-polk-county-o.text: A small Willamette Valley AVA in the hills of Polk County around an 835-foot peak.

wiki.title: Mount Pisgah, Polk County, Oregon AVA

united-states/mt-harlan.text: A high, inland Central Coast AVA of 1,800 to 2,200 feet in California's Gabilan Mountains, set apart from nearby lower-lying areas by its soil, elevation and microclimate. Its vineyards all belong to one winery, Calera, named for the old limestone lime kilns.

united-states/mt-veeder.text: A Napa Valley AVA in Napa County, high in the southern Mayacamas Mountains, with steep vineyards on thin, mostly sedimentary soils. Cabernet Sauvignon from here often shows briary flavors, moderate to bold tannins and herbal, floral aromas, in wines of powerful structure.

united-states/naches-heights.text: A very small Columbia Valley AVA in Washington's Yakima County, on the western edge of the Columbia Basin. Every vineyard is biodynamic or LIVE certified, and the vines are mostly Pinot Gris, with Sauvignon Blanc and Syrah.

united-states/napa-valley.text: California's first AVA and the nation's second, in a Mediterranean climate. Cabernet Sauvignon is the main grape in Napa County, followed by Chardonnay and Merlot. Napa gained wide recognition at the Paris Wine Tasting of 1976.

united-states/new-york.text: A US wine state, the third-largest grape-growing state by volume after California and Washington. Most of its vineyard area is American Vitis labrusca grapes, mainly Concord, and the rest is split between vinifera and French hybrids. Its AVAs include the Finger Lakes and Long Island.

united-states/niagara-escarpment.text: A narrow New York AVA along a free-draining limestone ridge near Lake Ontario, sharing terroir with Canada's Niagara Peninsula. Wines run from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay and Riesling to fruit wines, and the hybrid Traminette is grown in the county.

united-states/north-coast.text: A huge California AVA covering six counties north of San Francisco: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Sonoma and Solano. Its sub-appellations share weather shaped by Pacific fog and breezes.

united-states/north-fork.text: A Long Island AVA on a peninsula, with a maritime climate moderated by the Sound, Peconic Bay and the Atlantic. This lengthens the growing season by up to a month. Merlot, Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc are the most planted grapes.

wiki.title: North Fork of Long Island AVA

united-states/north-yuba.text: A Sierra Foothills AVA of volcanic soils in Yuba County, California, with terraced vineyards in the middle and upper foothills. Cabernet Sauvignon is the main grape, alongside Syrah, Grenache, Viognier and Roussanne.

united-states/northern-sonoma.text: A broad Sonoma County AVA covering the northern part of the county. It fully contains Alexander Valley, Russian River Valley, Dry Creek Valley and others. Its grapes include Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Zinfandel.

united-states/oak-knoll-district.text: A Napa Valley AVA at the southern end, near San Pablo Bay, with a climate cooler than any other Napa area except Carneros. It is planted largely to Merlot, Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon, and its Chardonnay has a reputation for a restrained, delicate style.

wiki.title: Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley AVA

united-states/oakville.text: A warm, flat Napa Valley AVA of well-drained gravelly and sandy loam between the Vaca and Mayacamas Mountains. It is known for Bordeaux grapes, which give wines of rich texture, firm tannins and notes of mint and herbs.

united-states/oregon.text: A US wine state where Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris are the top two grapes harvested. Pinot Noir commands the high end. Its two big AVAs are the Willamette Valley and Southern Oregon, and commercial winemaking began in the 1960s.

united-states/pacheco-pass.text: A small California AVA near Hollister, at the southern entrance to Pacheco Pass in Santa Clara and San Benito counties. It sits inside the Central Coast, Santa Clara Valley and San Francisco Bay AVAs, with only about 17 acres of vines when it was created.

united-states/paicines.text: A valley AVA in southwestern San Benito County, California, split from Monterey County by the Gabilan Mountains. The San Benito River runs through its vineyards. It is warmer than nearby San Benito areas but cooler than the Central Valley.

united-states/palos-verdes-peninsula.text: A tiny California AVA in Los Angeles County on the Pacific coast, bordered by the ocean on the west and south. It has two commercial vineyards and only about seven acres of vines in all, among suburban cities.

united-states/paso-robles.text: A large San Luis Obispo County AVA in California's Central Coast, known for Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon and Rhône-style wines. It contains eleven smaller districts, such as Adelaida, Creston and El Pomar.

united-states/paso-robles-estrella-distr.text: One of eleven districts inside the Paso Robles AVA, in San Luis Obispo County, California. It sits in the north-central part, northeast of the city of Paso Robles on both sides of the Estrella River watershed, with valleys and terraces.

united-states/paso-robles-geneseo-distri.text: A 17,300-acre district inside the Paso Robles AVA in California's Central Coast, just east of the city of Paso Robles and running to terraces along the Estrella River.

united-states/paso-robles-highlands-dist.text: A district of canyons and highlands inside the Paso Robles AVA, east of Creston. At 60,300 acres it is the second-largest in Paso Robles, reaching from near Shandon to the base of the La Panza Range.

united-states/paso-robles-willow-creek-d.text: A mountainous district inside the Paso Robles AVA, west of Highway 101 and bordering the Santa Lucia Range. It has a strong marine influence, a cool Winkler Region II growing season, elevations of 960 to 1,900 feet and 24 to 30 inches of rain a year.

wiki.title: Paso Robles Willow Creek District AVA

united-states/paulsell-valley.text: A small California AVA on the first rises out of the San Joaquin Valley floor, in Stanislaus County. It counts as Sierra Nevada foothills, with three vineyards on about 864 acres.

united-states/petaluma-gap.text: A Sonoma Coast AVA where a gap in the coastal mountains funnels cool Pacific fog and breezes inland to San Pablo Bay. The steady afternoon wind lowers yields. About 75 percent of plantings are Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and Syrah next.

united-states/pine-mountain-cloverdale-p.text: A small, high AVA of 1,600 to 2,600 feet at the northern end of the Mayacamas Range, straddling Mendocino and Sonoma counties. It is one of the most elevated grape-growing regions in California, near Cloverdale.

united-states/potter-valley.text: A Mendocino County valley AVA about 200 feet higher than its surroundings, near the Eel River watershed. Conditions favor botrytized wines, particularly Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and Semillon.

united-states/puget-sound.text: Washington's only AVA west of the Cascade Mountains, a wide basin around the Sound covering twelve counties in the northwest. Pinot Noir is the most planted grape here, ahead of Chardonnay and Pinot Gris.

united-states/ramona-valley.text: A broad, flat valley AVA in San Diego County, set in hills and mountains, with vineyards at about 1,400 feet and 16.5 inches of rain a year. It lies inside the South Coast AVA, and the county's main grapes are Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Merlot.

united-states/rattlesnake-hills.text: A Washington AVA in Yakima Valley, within the Columbia Valley, on a ridge where the AVA rises to 3,085 feet. Merlot is the most planted grape, followed by Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon.

united-states/red-hill-douglas-county-or.text: An AVA in Douglas County, Oregon, one of two sub-appellations of the Umpqua Valley, which sits in Southern Oregon.

united-states/red-hills-lake-county.text: A Lake County AVA of red, stony soils on rolling hills at the foot of Mount Konocti, beside Clear Lake. Elevations run from 1,400 to 3,000 feet.

united-states/red-mountain.text: A small Washington AVA of about 4,000 acres around Red Mountain in Benton County, inside Yakima Valley and the Columbia Valley. Its vineyards are planted mostly to red grapes, led by Cabernet Sauvignon at 64 percent, then Merlot and Syrah.

united-states/redwood-valley.text: A Mendocino County valley AVA, named for its redwood trees and sitting about 200 feet above its surroundings. It is cooler and needs a later harvest for ripeness. At one point it held around half of the county's vines.

united-states/ribbon-ridge.text: Oregon's smallest AVA, a 3,350-acre ridge at the northwest end of the Chehalem Mountains in the Willamette Valley. About 90 percent of its vineyards are planted to Pinot Noir, which is aromatic with good structure, bright acidity and a salty, seashell mineral note.

united-states/river-junction.text: A small AVA in California, at the confluence of the San Joaquin and Stanislaus Rivers in San Joaquin County. It is cooler than the rest of the Central Valley and is the only place in the valley with lots of fine sandy loam. About 90 percent of it is planted to Chardonnay.

united-states/rockpile.text: A small AVA in the northwestern part of Sonoma County, beside Lake Sonoma, with about 160 acres of vines at or above 800 feet. It overlaps the northwestern corner of the Dry Creek Valley appellation and sits within Northern Sonoma.

united-states/rocky-reach.text: A strip of land along the Columbia River in central Washington, between Chelan and Wenatchee, entirely within the Columbia Valley AVA. It has seven vineyards on about 117 acres. The name comes from a rocky stretch of river rapids.

united-states/rogue-valley.text: A large Southern Oregon AVA covering the Rogue River valley and its tributary valleys, such as the Applegate. It is the warmest and driest of Oregon's wine regions, and Pinot Noir is its most planted grape, followed by Pinot Gris.

united-states/royal-slope.text: A Columbia Valley AVA in central Washington, around the town of Royal City between the Quincy Basin and the Saddle Mountains. It has 13 vineyards on about 1,900 acres.

united-states/russian-river-valley.text: A cool Sonoma County AVA between Sebastopol and Santa Rosa to the south and Healdsburg to the north, shaped by fog from the nearby Pacific Ocean. It is known for cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

united-states/rutherford.text: A Napa Valley AVA in the center of the valley, known for its Cabernet Sauvignon. Its well-drained soils mix gravel, loam and sand with volcanic deposits and marine sediments. It is home to historic wineries such as Beaulieu Vineyards and Inglenook.

united-states/saddle-rock-malibu.text: A small AVA of about 2,090 acres in the Santa Monica Mountains of western Los Angeles County, with 85 acres of vineyards at 1,800 to 2,000 feet. It is named for a saddle-shaped rock and, since 2014, sits within the Malibu Coast AVA.

united-states/salado-creek.text: A tiny AVA on the western edge of California's Central Valley, in Stanislaus County, at the base of the Diablo Range. It had only 44 acres of vines when created, mostly small growers selling to wineries outside the area.

united-states/san-antonio-valley.text: A warm, dry Central Coast AVA in the Santa Lucia Range of Monterey County, around Lake San Antonio. Gravelly loam and clay soils and a climate like Paso Robles suit full-bodied Rhône and Bordeaux grapes, and more than 20 varieties are grown.

united-states/san-benito.text: A Central Coast AVA along the San Benito River near Hollister, with a moderate climate cooled by Pacific breezes. It contains Paicines, Cienega Valley and Lime Kiln Valley. About 23 grape varieties grow here, and it once supplied most grapes for Almadén Vineyards.

united-states/san-bernabe.text: A Monterey AVA in the Salinas Valley between the Salinas River and the Santa Lucia Mountains, mostly rolling hills with sandy soils. About 5,000 acres of vines sit on a single vineyard.

united-states/san-francisco-bay.text: A multi-county Central Coast AVA around the San Francisco Bay Area, covering the South and East Bay counties. Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon lead plantings, and it contains Livermore Valley and Santa Clara Valley.

united-states/san-juan-creek.text: One of the two easternmost districts inside the Paso Robles AVA, following the San Juan Creek valley at 980 to 1,600 feet. It sits in the rain shadow of the Santa Lucia Coast Range, so it is warmer and more continental than the western districts.

united-states/san-lucas.text: A Monterey AVA at the southern end of the Salinas Valley around the town of San Lucas, set apart from neighbors mainly by its microclimate. Its vineyards run from alluvial fans and terraces to low hills up to 800 feet.

united-states/san-luis-obispo-coast.text: A cool coastal Central Coast AVA between the Santa Lucia Mountains and the Pacific, about 70 miles long. Most vineyards lie within six miles of the ocean, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay commonly grown. Its alternate name is SLO Coast.

united-states/san-luis-rey.text: A San Diego County AVA inside the South Coast AVA, stretching from the coast at Oceanside inland to the Merriam Mountains. It has 44 commercial vineyards on about 256 acres, and its identity rests on topography, climate and soils.

united-states/san-miguel-district.text: One of the two northernmost districts of the Paso Robles AVA, around the town of San Miguel on the Monterey County line. It has a very mild marine influence, only 11.4 inches of rain and a warm Winkler Region III climate, on alluvial fans and terraces.

united-states/san-pasqual-valley.text: A narrow, 9,000-acre valley AVA in northern San Diego County, running inland from Escondido. It was the nation's fifth AVA and the county's first, and sits within the South Coast AVA.

united-states/san-ysidro-district.text: A cool AVA in southern Santa Clara County, east of Gilroy, inside the Santa Clara Valley. Breezes come up the Pajaro River. It was set up around two vineyards, Mistral and San Ysidro, with about 520 acres under vine.

united-states/santa-clara-valley.text: An AVA from southern San Francisco Bay down to Gilroy and Morgan Hill, important in early California wine and home to pioneers Paul Masson and Charles Lefranc. It contains the Pacheco Pass and San Ysidro District AVAs.

united-states/santa-cruz-mountains.text: A Central Coast mountain AVA across Santa Clara, Santa Cruz and San Mateo counties, one of the first defined by its topography. It follows the coastal fog line, and elevation, fog, sun and soil create many microclimates. In those three counties Pinot Noir and Chardonnay lead plantings.

united-states/santa-lucia-highlands.text: A Central Coast AVA in Monterey County on the eastern flank of the Santa Lucia Mountains, with vineyards up to 1,200 feet, about half planted to Pinot Noir. Cool morning fog and Monterey Bay breezes give way to warm afternoons on sun-facing slopes.

united-states/santa-margarita-ranch.text: The southernmost district of the Paso Robles AVA, ringing the town of Santa Margarita against the Santa Lucia Mountains and set apart from the other ten districts. Syrah has played a pivotal role, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, Merlot, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay also grown.

united-states/santa-maria-valley.text: A south Central Coast AVA straddling Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties, the nation's third AVA. Its east-west valley lets cool Pacific wind and fog flow in, giving a mild climate and a longer growing season. Chardonnay and Pinot Noir are the leading grapes in the county.

united-states/santa-ynez-valley.text: A Central Coast AVA in Santa Barbara County with the most wineries in the county, in an east-west corridor between the Santa Ynez and San Rafael Mountains. It is very cool near the coast and warmer inland. Chardonnay is the main grape in the cooler west, and Rhône grapes do well in the east.

united-states/seiad-valley.text: A tiny AVA in Siskiyou County in northwestern California, beside the Klamath River near the Oregon border. It covered just 2.5 acres of vines and one winery, which has since closed, so the appellation now exists only on paper.

united-states/seneca-lake.text: A Finger Lakes AVA around Seneca Lake, a glacial lake about 35 miles long and up to 600 feet deep. The lake does not freeze, so it stores heat and lengthens the growing season. Riesling is the most commercially important grape.

united-states/sierra-foothills.text: A vast, 160-mile-long AVA in the Sierra Nevada foothills of north-central California, planted to wine grapes since the Gold Rush of 1849. Zinfandel is the main grape in the area's counties, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah.

united-states/sierra-pelona-valley.text: A small California valley AVA in the Sierra Pelona Mountains of northwestern Los Angeles County, around Agua Dulce. Grapes have been grown here only since 1995, and by 2008 there were 96 acres of commercial vineyards.

united-states/sloughhouse.text: A Lodi sub-AVA in Sacramento County, about 21 miles southeast of Sacramento, covering 78,800 acres. It is one of seven smaller areas carved from the Lodi AVA in 2006.

united-states/snipes-mountain.text: A small Washington AVA of about 4,145 acres near Outlook in the Yakima Valley, the state's third smallest. It has one of Washington's oldest vineyard histories, and Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot are the leading grapes.

united-states/solano-county-green-valley.text: A small North Coast valley AVA in Solano County, east of Napa Valley, about one mile wide and four miles long between the Vaca Mountains and the Mount George Range. Solano County is added to the name to tell it apart from Green Valley in Sonoma. Chardonnay is the county's main grape.

united-states/sonoma-coast.text: A huge Sonoma County AVA of about 480,000 acres along the Pacific coast and some inland areas. It is cool and rainy compared with the rest of the county, with so many microclimates that smaller coastal AVAs such as Fort Ross-Seaview and West Sonoma Coast were carved from it.

united-states/sonoma-county.text: One of California's largest wine grape producers, far outproducing the Napa Valley AVA. Its main grapes are Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon. It holds many AVAs, such as Russian River Valley, Alexander Valley and Dry Creek Valley.

united-states/sonoma-mountain.text: A hillside AVA on the western edge of the Valley of the Moon in southern Sonoma County, around a 2,463-foot mountain and the town of Glen Ellen. Many microclimates in its folds and ridges suit Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Semillon and Zinfandel.

united-states/sonoma-valley.text: A southeastern Sonoma County AVA, whose name means Valley of the Moon, with 13,000 acres of vines between the Mayacamas Mountains and the Sonoma Mountains. It contains the Moon Mountain District.

united-states/south-coast.text: A big Southern California AVA across five counties, from Los Angeles to the Mexican border. Its sub-appellations share warm weather moderated by cool Pacific influences.

united-states/southern-oregon.text: A "super-AVA" in southwest Oregon that joins the Rogue Valley and Umpqua Valley so the two regions can market together. Pinot Noir is the most planted grape, followed by Pinot Gris, Syrah and Chardonnay.

united-states/spring-mountain-district.text: A Napa Valley sub-appellation of mostly east-facing hillside vineyards, its boundary running from 400 to 2,600 feet. Small hillside yields mean it makes under 2 percent of Napa Valley wine.

united-states/squaw-valley-miramonte.text: A rural California AVA in the Sierra Nevada foothills of Fresno County, east of the city of Fresno, with no overlap with other AVAs. It covers 44,690 acres but has only five vineyards on about 7.5 acres and three wineries.

united-states/st-helena.text: A Napa Valley AVA in Napa County around the town of St. Helena, about sixteen miles northwest of the city of Napa.

united-states/sta-rita-hills.text: A Central Coast AVA in Santa Barbara County on the western edge of the Santa Ynez Valley, enclosed by it but separate. Its name was shortened from Santa Rita Hills in 2006 after a protest from a Chilean producer.

united-states/stags-leap-district.text: A small Napa Valley AVA, only about one by three miles, noted for Cabernet Sauvignon and Petite Sirah. Clay loam from the Napa River and volcanic soil from the Vaca Mountains set it apart. A 1973 Stag's Leap Cabernet ranked first at the 1976 Judgment of Paris.

united-states/suisun-valley.text: A North Coast valley AVA in Solano County, west of Fairfield and east of Napa Valley, about three miles wide and eight miles long. It grows more than twenty grape varieties on about 3,000 acres, from Barbera and Cabernet Sauvignon to Viognier and Zinfandel.

united-states/tehachapi-mountains.text: A California AVA around the town of Tehachapi in Kern County, between the Tehachapi Mountains and the southern Sierra Nevada. It is small, with six vineyards on 25 acres in 2020.

united-states/temecula-valley.text: A Riverside County AVA on the eastern slopes of the Santa Ana Mountains, inside the South Coast AVA. About 5,000 of its 33,000 acres sit in a protected Citrus and Vineyard Zone. Cabernet Sauvignon is the main grape in the county.

united-states/templeton-gap-district.text: A district of the Paso Robles AVA that encircles the town of Templeton, named for erosional gaps along the crest of the Santa Lucia Range to the west. It holds about 1,600 acres of vineyards.

united-states/the-burn-of-columbia-valle.text: A Columbia Valley AVA in Washington known locally as The Burn, on the north bank of the Columbia River along the Oregon border in Klickitat County. Three vineyards farm about 1,261 acres, and many Washington wineries source grapes here. It sits between the Columbia Gorge and Horse Heaven Hills.

wiki.title: The Burn of Columbia Valley AVA

united-states/the-hamptons.text: A Long Island AVA covering the South Fork, bounded by the Atlantic and Peconic Bay. It is cooler and foggier than the North Fork, on silt and loam soils. Only three wineries and vineyards operate there as of 2025.

united-states/the-rocks-district-of-milt.text: An Oregon AVA inside the Walla Walla Valley and the wider Columbia Valley, defined by its soil: an alluvial fan covered in baseball-sized basalt cobbles. It is described as the only US AVA whose boundaries follow soil type, and its wines are said to get unique flavors from the volcanic rocks.

wiki.title: The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater AVA

united-states/tracy-hills.text: A California AVA on the western edge of the Central Valley, on the low Altamont Hills around Tracy. It has limited rain, persistent winds and little fog. Its best-known wines are Italian varieties such as Nero d'Avola, Montepulciano and Sagrantino.

united-states/trinity-lakes.text: A north-central California AVA around two man-made lakes, Trinity Lake and Lewiston Lake, among steep timbered ridges and narrow valleys. The lakes cool the days and warm the nights. Only 30 acres were planted in 2005, with two wineries.

united-states/tualatin-hills.text: An Oregon AVA in the northernmost Willamette Valley, west of Portland, in the upland hills of the Tualatin River watershed at 200 to 1,000 feet.

united-states/umpqua-valley.text: A Douglas County AVA in Southern Oregon with 70 vineyards on about 4,000 acres. Pinot Noir is the main grape, at 76 percent of plantings, with Pinot Gris, Tempranillo and Syrah behind. It holds Red Hill Douglas County and Elkton Oregon.

united-states/upper-hudson.text: A large upstate New York AVA northwest of Albany, covering about 960,000 acres across seven counties. At the outset it had only about 67 acres of vines on 19 vineyards.

united-states/upper-lake-valley.text: A valley AVA north of Clear Lake in Lake County, set 1,326 to 2,820 feet up among valleys south of the Mendocino National Forest. It started with 16 vineyards on about 300 acres.

united-states/van-duzer-corridor.text: A Willamette Valley AVA in Yamhill and Polk counties, northwest of Salem, on the 45th parallel. It has about 18 vineyards.

united-states/wahluke-slope.text: A Columbia Valley AVA in Grant County, Washington, near Mattawa. It is primarily known for Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, and Cabernet is 47 percent of plantings.

united-states/walla-walla-valley.text: A Columbia Valley AVA straddling southeast Washington and northeast Oregon. After Yakima Valley it has the most vineyards and wineries in Washington, about 140 wineries and tasting rooms. Cabernet Sauvignon is over half of plantings, then Syrah and Merlot.

united-states/washington.text: The second-largest wine-producing US state, with 99.9 percent of wine grape production in the dry eastern half, in the Cascade rain shadow with about 8 inches of rain and long sunlight hours. Irrigation is key. Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot lead the red plantings.

united-states/west-sonoma-coast.text: A Sonoma County AVA of 141,846 acres on the coast, in a Marine zone climate, which includes the Fort Ross-Seaview AVA. It has about 47 commercial vineyards on roughly 1,028 acres.

united-states/white-bluffs.text: A Columbia Valley AVA on plateaus overlooking the Columbia River in Franklin County, Washington, about 10 miles north of the Tri-Cities. It began with nine vineyards on about 1,127 acres and one winery.

united-states/wild-horse-valley.text: A small valley AVA straddling Napa and Solano counties, partly inside Napa Valley. Its petitioners described more sun than nearby areas and cooling from San Pablo Bay. It had only 73 acres under vine when created.

united-states/willamette-valley.text: Oregon's largest AVA, covering the Willamette River basin, with a cool, moist climate and worldwide recognition for Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir is 72 percent of plantings, then Pinot Gris. Eyrie Vineyard's showing at the 1979 Wine Olympics first brought it attention.

united-states/willow-creek.text: One of the oldest, smallest and northernmost active AVAs in California, a narrow 6,000-acre valley cut by the Trinity River in the Klamath Mountains. It is rugged, with lots of sunlight and heat. By 2008 it had no bonded wineries and only ten acres of vines.

united-states/winters-highlands.text: A small California AVA in the easternmost foothills of the northern Coast Range, in Solano and Yolo counties, next to the city of Winters. It has about 134 acres of vines and three wineries, growing Petite Sirah, Tempranillo, Malbec and Chardonnay.
